newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares end lower after hectic OTC trade.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares end lower after hectic OTC trade.

text.p: Singapore stocks turned mildly bearish in active trade on Monday as funds adjusted their positions following a re-rating of some blue chip issues.
Dealers said institutional investors were heavy sellers from early in the day, spurred by a new weighting of the Morgan Stanley Capital International (MSCI) Singapore Free Index.
Among net losers were the foreign tranches of the top four local banks OCBC, UOB, DBS and OUB, down by between S$1.40 and 40 cents, on the changes to the index.
Investors also relinquished properties, hurt by negative comments last week from Finance Minister Richard Hu.
The Straits Times Industrials Index fell 7.29 points to 2,233.99 on a buoyant volume of 478.4 million shares.

"This whole thing about the weighting of MSCI will filter through. It's not reflective of what's happening in the market," a dealer with a foreign brokerage said, noting the 0.41 point fall in the exchange's foreign index to 119.67, was meager.
Small capitalisation issues were the mainstay of overall volume with Malaysian stocks heading the top 10 actives.
Malaysia's Insas Bhd saw 27 million shares traded, reaching a new high at Singapore $1.35. It ended at $1.32, up S$0.06.
